articles.body: Key takeaways LLM observability and LLM visibility are unrelated products sold under overlapping search terms. This is about the second one. Citation overlap between engines on the same prompt runs under 30%, so a pooled six-engine average can hide being invisible on the engine your category actually uses. Build-versus-buy flips around 50,000 queries a month or 10 tracked clients. Below 5,000 a dashboard wins on time-to-value alone. First, a disambiguation that wastes a lot of people's time. LLM observability is telemetry for models your application calls: tokens, latency, traces, cost. Datadog, LangSmith, Helicone. LLM visibility is what models say about your brand: whether ChatGPT names you, which sources it cites, how you move against competitors. Same search terms, unrelated products.

articles.title: Rate Limiting in the Next.js App Router: Field Notes on Middleware, Redis, and the Server Action That Looks Like Every Other POST
articles.excerpt: Headline: An in-memory rate limiter is wrong on serverless because every function instance keeps its own counter, so a limit of 10 requests per minute becomes 10 requests per minute per instance. The…
articles.body: Headline: An in-memory rate limiter is wrong on serverless because every function instance keeps its own counter, so a limit of 10 requests per minute becomes 10 requests per minute per instance . The second trap is that every Next.js Server Action POSTs to the URL of the page that called it, so path-based limiting in middleware cannot tell one action from another. A rate limiter is a counter with a deadline: allow N requests per identity per time window and reject the rest with HTTP 429. I have written that in ten lines before and been happy with it. Moving the same idea into a Next.js 16 App Router project on Vercel broke it in three places I did not expect — where the counter lives, who counts as an identity, and how you attach a limit to a Server Action that has no URL of its own.

articles.title: Un system prompt se reconstitue à partir d'une seule réponse
articles.excerpt: L'essentiel Des chercheurs de l'IIT Bombay et d'Adobe Research reconstituent le prompt d'origine à partir du seul texte produit par un modèle, sans accès à ses poids. Leur méthode, baptisée « Previous…
articles.body: L'essentiel Des chercheurs de l'IIT Bombay et d'Adobe Research reconstituent le prompt d'origine à partir du seul texte produit par un modèle, sans accès à ses poids. Leur méthode, baptisée « Previous-Token Prediction », entraîne un modèle inverse qui prédit les tokens précédents au lieu du suivant. Un modèle inverse entraîné sur le petit Qwen-3-0.6B retrouve le sens de prompts envoyés à GPT-4o : savoir quel modèle a répondu n'est même pas nécessaire. La démonstration porte sur des prompts d'une à deux phrases ; les system prompts longs n'ont pas été testés. Une réponse suffit. Pas les paramètres internes du modèle, pas les logs du fournisseur, pas la moindre clé d'API : le texte produit, et rien d'autre, permet de remonter à la consigne qui l'a déclenché.

articles.title: Why "true or false" is the wrong question for media literacy tools
articles.excerpt: Tagi: #media #ai #discuss Most tools built to fight misinformation return a verdict: true, false,misleading. I want to argue that this framing is the reason they mostlyfail to convince the people who…
articles.body: Tagi: #media #ai #discuss Most tools built to fight misinformation return a verdict: true, false,misleading. I want to argue that this framing is the reason they mostlyfail to convince the people who need them most. The trust paradox To accept a fact-checker's verdict, you must already trust the fact-checker. For a reader convinced that media are biased, a "this is false" label is notinformation — it is one more voice from the side they already distrust.The tool cannot work on the audience it was built for. This is not a technology problem. Better models will not fix it, becausethe obstacle is structural: a verdict demands trust before it delivers value. What changes when you stop giving verdicts An alternative framing: instead of judging the content, describe its structure.

articles.title: Touchdown! Private Chinese rocket aces landing on 2nd-ever flight
articles.excerpt: The Beijing-based company LandSpace landed its Zhuque-3 rocket this evening (Aug. 18), notching a huge milestone for commercial Chinese spaceflight.
articles.body: China just notched another big spaceflight milestone. The Beijing startup LandSpace successfully landed the first stage of its Zhuque-3 rocket this evening (Aug. 18), becoming the first Chinese company ever to do so during an orbital launch. It was just the second Chinese orbital rocket touchdown overall. The first was pulled of on July 10 by a Long March 10B , which is built by the state-owned China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). The Long March 10B had some help returning to Earth, settling softly into a net-like device affixed to a ship at sea. But Zhuque-3 came down on terra firma and stayed upright thanks to a set of landing legs, like those sported by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9 rocket.
